image_description: A large sturgeon fish swimming in an aquarium tank, viewed through glass. The fish has an elongated fusiform body with visible bony scutes along its back and sides. The water is clear with a sandy/rocky bottom visible. Another fish is partially visible in the background.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated head with protrusible mouth on ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is clearly elongated and the mouth appears to be positioned on the ventral (underside) surface, consistent with sturgeon anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Four barbels (sensory whiskers) anterior to mouth.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The barbels are not clearly visible in this image due to the angle and water clarity. The area anterior to the mouth is somewhat obscured.
The snout is clearly pointed and elongated, matching sturgeon characteristics.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated fusiform body with impressively large, extended proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body is clearly elongated and fusiform (tapered at both ends), with large proportions typical of sturgeon.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Five rows of bony scutes (plates) along body instead of scales.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Multiple rows of bony scutes are clearly visible along the dorsal and lateral surfaces of the fish. While counting exactly five rows is difficult from this angle, the presence of scutes instead of scales is evident.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Gray, brown, or black dorsally with lighter ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal surface appears dark gray/brown while the ventral surface is noticeably lighter, matching the expected coloration.
The tail fin is clearly visible and shows the characteristic asymmetrical (heterocercal) structure with the upper lobe longer than the lower lobe.

artifact_observations.location: Body surface, particularly along the scutes
artifact_observations.reasoning: Slight inconsistency in the texture of the scutes - some appear slightly too smooth or uniform compared to natural variation. Minor edge bleeding between scutes and body surface.
Minor perspective warping in the background elements, particularly the second fish which appears slightly distorted. The tank glass also creates some refraction artifacts.
